description:
Every certificate issued for one public key, by the key's SHA-256 (spki_sha256 on a certificate). NEEDS AN API KEY ON THE PLUS PLAN OR ABOVE.

Key reuse across certificates for unrelated names is a strong operator linkage. It searches only certificates first observed in the last 32 hours (the live table); archived certificates are not searched by key, and certificates ingested before 2026-09-07 carry no key hash. So a short answer can mean "not searched" rather than "not reused"; the reply's coverage field says so.

Get the hash from get_certificate (spki_sha256). Returns up to 50 certificates; truncated true means there are more. To see one of them in full pass its cert_id to get_certificate.

spki_sha256.description: The 64-hex SHA-256 of the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, exactly as get_certificate reports it in spki_sha256. Case does not matter. Not the certificate's own SHA-256, which identifies one certificate rather than its key.
